sections.description: This section details the comprehensive history and subjective symptoms of the patient, highlighting the long-standing nature of her neurological complaints, their impact on quality of life, and the progressive timeline connecting trauma, headache onset, and subsequent choking/hypoxia episodes.
subtopics: Chronic Pain and Headache Characteristics: 14-year history of vertex/occipital headache and allodynia.
Bulbar and Dysphagia Symptoms: Choking episodes affecting solids and liquids with no complete obstruction.
Hypoxia Monitoring: Asymptomatic oxygen desaturation (70-80%) and its discovery via home monitoring.
Precipitating Events: Motor vehicle accident 14 years prior and subsequent symptom latency.
Social and Psychological Impact: Avoidance behaviors and emotional distress from frequent public choking events.

sections.section_title: Neurophysiology of Respiratory Dysfunction in Chiari Malformation
sections.description: This section explains the underlying mechanisms by which Chiari Malformation Type I (CMI) leads to respiratory compromise, distinguishing the physical anatomical alterations from the functional disruption of brainstem respiratory control centers.
subtopics: Cerebellar Tonsillar Descent and CSF Flow Obstruction: The volumetric mismatch in a small posterior fossa.
Brainstem Compression and Automatic Breathing: Mechanism of acquired central hypoventilation syndrome.
Preserved Voluntary vs. Impaired Automatic Control: Why patients do not experience dyspnea during desaturation.
Lower Cranial Nerve Involvement: Mechanisms behind choking (cricopharyngeal achalasia vs. other mechanisms).

sections.description: This section outlines the stepwise diagnostic reasoning used to reach the unifying diagnosis, emphasizing the value of historical imaging review, exclusion of common misdiagnoses, and the specific utility of MRI and polysomnography in this context.
subtopics: Exclusionary Gastroenterology and Otolaryngology: Results of normal laryngoscopies and endoscopies.
Comparative Pulmonary Evaluation: Normal pulmonary function tests and chest imaging.
The Crucial Role of Historical Imaging: Re-evaluating the 14-year-old CT scan of the head.
Polygraphy Interpretation: Analysis of the sleep study showing predominant central events (72%).
Definitive Diagnosis: MRI confirmation of 11 mm cerebellar tonsillar descent.

sections.description: This section covers the treatment algorithm for symptomatic CMI, discussing the specific options presented in this case, balancing surgical decompression risks against the patient's preference for conservative management.
subtopics: Surgical Decompression: Posterior fossa decompression as definitive treatment for CSF flow disturbance.
Conservative Management: Dietary modifications and coping strategies.

sections.description: This section synthesizes the case into actionable clinical guidelines for future practitioners, focusing on the importance of history taking, differential diagnosis of dysphagia, and long-term surveillance strategies.
subtopics: Diagnostic Pitfalls: Recognizing CMI in patients with unexplained central hypoventilation.
Differential Diagnosis Convergence: Distinguishing CMI from acquired vs. congenital central hypoventilation.
Surveillance and Monitoring: Monthly assessments and periodic MRI surveillance.
The Importance of Vertex Symptoms: Clinical significance of scalp allodynia in CMI.
Limitations of Bedside Sleep Testing and Future Directions.
